name: Magic Formulas
description: People in the Tomskaya region like magic formulas very much. You can see some of them below. Imagine you are given a sequence of positive integer numbers p 1 , p 2 , ..., p n . input_specification: The first line of the input contains the only integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 6 ). The next line contains n integers: p 1 , p 2 , ..., p n ( 0 ≤ p i ≤ 2·10 9 ).
output_specification: The only line of output should contain a single integer — the value of Q .
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 424C — Magic Formulas [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
